claims.evidence: The 'Cyberleek' is threatening its biggest Grand Theft Auto 6 leak yet, if its demands aren't met

claims.claim: A message on the leaker's website says a build of GTA 6 will be released, with the full story mode played to the end, if the leaker's cryptocurrency reaches a $30 million market cap.
claims.evidence: IGN reports the site was updated with a warning tied to a $30 million market cap and reproduces the message.

claims.claim: The message says Take-Two can stop the release by issuing the game on physical discs and apologising publicly.
claims.evidence: IGN reproduces the message.
claims.quote: Take-Two gets one way out: physical disks and a public apology.

claims.claim: IGN says it is unclear whether the leaker means to release a build of the game or a video of a full playthrough.
claims.evidence: IGN: unclear whether Cyberleek intends to release a build online or a full playthrough in video form.

claims.claim: IGN put the coin's market cap at $3.8 million when its article was published, after a peak of $5.7 million earlier that day, and called $30 million unlikely.
claims.evidence: IGN: market cap of $3.8 million at publication, spiked at $5.7 million; seems unlikely to get near $30 million.

claims.claim: Polygon, a day later, put the coin's market cap at $6 million and said it had been rising since the message appeared.
claims.evidence: Polygon: sits at a $6 million market cap as of writing, rising since the offer went live.

claims.claim: The leaker also tied lower market cap targets to footage of the character Lucia in fewer clothes.
claims.evidence: IGN: market cap goals tied to the clothing Lucia would wear in subsequent leaked gameplay.

claims.claim: The leaker went quiet after a run of leaks in August and returned this week with a gameplay video of about 24 minutes.
claims.evidence: IGN: appeared to go dark after August leaks; reemerged this week with a 24-minute gameplay video.

claims.claim: Eurogamer says it has seen this week's video and that it appears to be legitimate.
claims.evidence: Eurogamer: has seen the video, and it appears to be legitimate.

claims.claim: Rockstar has previously called the leaks heartbreaking and said this was not how it intended players to see the game.
claims.evidence: Eurogamer quotes Rockstar's earlier statements.
claims.quote: this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time

claims.claim: GTA 6 is due on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on 19 November.
claims.evidence: Eurogamer: due out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on 19th November.

claims.claim: Take-Two subpoenaed Discord and Microsoft in August for user records connected to the posting and spread of the leaked videos, and there has been no public update on what was handed over.
claims.evidence: Kotaku: subpoenaed Discord and Microsoft in August; no update since on what Discord handed over.

claims.claim: Kotaku reports the leaker's account appeared to withdraw about $250,000 of its coin in late August, after which the coin crashed.
claims.evidence: Kotaku: went quiet in late August after seemingly withdrawing $250,000 worth of its meme coin, leading to the scheme's immediate crash.

claims.claim: IGN reports that analysis of transactions in late August pointed to the leaker cashing out around $270,000.
claims.evidence: IGN: analysis pointed to the leaker having cashed out, earning around $270,000.

claims.claim: Kotaku describes the new threat as looking like a second round of a rug pull.
claims.evidence: Kotaku: this latest threat just looks like round two of the rug pull.

claims.claim: Kotaku says nothing more is known about who operates the account or who they work with.
claims.evidence: Kotaku: we still don't know anything else about who is operating the Cyberleek account.

claims.claim: VGC describes the threat as a promise to leak a working build of the game.
claims.evidence: VGC: it will leak a working build of GTA 6.

claims.claim: The group has said its leaks are a protest against GTA 6 being sold without a physical version, while also promoting a crypto scheme.
claims.evidence: VGC: claimed leaks were in protest of digital pre-orders and no physical version; it has also been promoting a crypto scheme.

claims.claim: Take-Two has filed several subpoenas to Discord and withdrew a separate subpoena request to YouTube, telling the court it no longer needed that information.
claims.evidence: VGC quotes Take-Two's legal representative.
claims.quote: Take-Two has determined it no longer needs the particular information requested

claims.claim: Polygon considers it highly unlikely that Take-Two will meet the demands this close to launch.
claims.evidence: Polygon: highly unlikely that Take-Two will meet the leaker's demands, especially so close to launch.

conflicts.description: IGN (about $270,000) and Kotaku (about $250,000) give different figures for the August withdrawal.
IGN says it is unclear whether a build or a video playthrough is threatened; VGC describes a working build.
